subject: RFP: Audit log handoff format, bulk export and LLM-aware redaction guidance

Subject: RFP: Audit log handoff format, bulk export and LLM-aware redaction guidance

Diego,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. AuroraHealth is finalizing a vendor RFP focused on audit trail preservation and bulk exportability for systems that may pipeline data into our internal ML validators. A few specifics we need answered for the RFP matrix:

1) Supported audit export formats (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV, raw structured events) and schema stability guarantees.
2) Retention windows per log class and whether per-account retention policies are available.
3) For bulk handoffs: maximum single-export size, pagination/stream semantics, and integrity verification (checksums, manifest).
4) Controls for redaction when audit events may contain model prompts or LLM-generated content — do you provide deterministic redaction tooling or redaction metadata to support downstream ML analysis?
5) Time to produce a full evidence bundle (including chain-of-custody metadata) for legal hold — SLA expectations.

We intend to include any vendor attachments (sample manifest, schema, example export) directly in the RFP response. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an export sample and a short playbook describing export procedures and LLM-aware redaction best practices by next Wednesday (May 26)?

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Sr. Procurement Manager
AuroraHealth Systems

Subject: Re: RFP: Audit log handoff format, bulk export and LLM-aware redaction guidance

Claire—

Appreciate the clear list. We can absolutely provide the deliverables you described. High-level answers up front, and we’ll attach a compact playbook and sample export for the RFP:

1) Formats: NDJSON (primary for event streams), Parquet (columnar snapshots), CSV (summary exports). Our export manifests include a schema version and field-level typing; we maintain backward-compatible schema evolution guarantees for two major releases and document change logs.

2) Retention: Per-account retention policies supported (customer-configurable up to 10 years), with predefined classes (auth-events, admin-audit, inference-requests, model-ops). Short-term cache/eviction differs from long-term archival. We can support legal-hold overrides to extend retention immediately.

3) Bulk handoff: Exports are streamed via signed S3 upload (pre-signed multipart) or delivered to your SFTP. Single-export logical bundles currently support up to 5 TB; we shard larger exports into numbered parts with manifest. Each bundle includes SHA256 checksums and a JWS-signed manifest for integrity + provenance.

4) LLM-aware redaction: We offer three modes — none, token-level masked redaction (deterministic removal of PII with redaction markers), and metadata-only redaction (retain redaction metadata and hashed tokens for ML use). We also provide an optional redaction report that lists redaction decisions and a redaction confidence score per event to enable downstream auditing and ML validation.

5) Evidence bundle SLA: Standard turnaround for a production tenant is 5 business days for a complete evidence bundle; expedited (48 hours) available under contract for high-priority legal holds. Bundles include export files, manifest, checksum, chain-of-custody events, and a delivery receipt.

We’ll attach the playbook and a small sample NDJSON extract demonstrating redaction metadata and an export manifest. Marissa and Kimberly are looped on technical details. If you’d like, we can schedule a short call to walk through the sample on Wednesday morning.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Diego / Kim —

Quick notes to prep for the call:

• Token-preserving redaction: We can produce masked outputs that keep original token counts by replacing tokens with mask tokens of equal byte-length when required; we should document the tokenization assumptions (we use BPE/byte-level tokenizers depending on model family). If Aurora requires exact alignment, recommend an initial calibration export for their ML pipeline to verify tokenizers.

• Manifest signing: Default flow uses Redwood-managed signing keys (we sign the manifest server-side and include the key id). We support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) for an additional attestation step — when enabled, the export manifest is signed with a customer key via an HSM-backed flow and key rotation metadata is captured in the manifest.

Action items for call:
1) Diego — walk sample NDJSON and show redaction metadata fields (redaction_type, redaction_span, redaction_confidence).
2) Kim — confirm KMS onboarding steps and provide the required IAM permission checklist.
3) Marissa — confirm SLA language & expedited cost schedule.

I’ll take lead on the sample walkthrough.

Thanks,

Claire —

Thanks for the clarifying questions — answers below and attached the small sample/guide: redwood-audit-export-playbook.pdf and llm-redaction-guidelines.docx. We also uploaded a sanitized NDJSON sample (sample-audit-slice-ndjson.jsonl) showing the three redaction modes.

• Token counts: Our masked redaction preserves token counts when requested by substituting per-token mask placeholders and including a token_alignment field in each event. We’ll include a short calibration script in the playbook to verify tokenizer parity.

• Signing keys: By default we sign manifests using Redwood-managed keys (we include key id and timestamp in the manifest). If Aurora requires KMS-managed signing, we support an HSM-backed signing integration; the process requires a key import or cross-account KMS grant and takes ~3 business days to validate for a new tenant. The playbook contains the IAM checklist.

Call: 09:00 PT tomorrow works for us — joining link: https://meet.redwood.com/meet/aurora-rfp-0526 (calendar invite sent).
